title: Gate reading level only on your texts
statement: Gate a reading-level band only on texts you wrote; on published texts you chose, measure and report it, since they are not yours to rewrite to a number.
detail: A reading engine's rule pack gives its reading-level band two uses, measuring any passage and gating one only when the course wrote it, after an earlier generator spent whole refine budgets enforcing a Lexile target on folktales that were never going to reach it. Its copy rules exempt story prose from the 25-word sentence ceiling for the same reason, since editing a narrative sentence down to hit a number is the Lexile-driven editing its knowledge rules forbid. It matches the rule that a lesson changes to fit its fixed source text, never the reverse (fix-the-lesson-never-the-source).
against: A crosswalk for adopting a partner's texts took the other line after finding that they averaged Flesch-Kincaid grade 9.7: "Every prose text we adopted therefore carries a logged commitment: re-leveled to the Grade-4 band before authoring, with the original kept as the source." (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/extras/g4-crosswalk-2026-08-17.md`, line 82). The record text-within-the-grades-reading-band also asks that every passage sit within or just above its grade's band.

evidence.quote: A band for MEASURING a passage, and for gating one only when we wrote it. gen_v3 spent whole refine budgets enforcing a Lexile target on folktales that were never going to reach it; a published text the academics team chose is not ours to rewrite to a number.
**Story prose.** Literature at grades 4 to 6 runs longer than anything else a child reads. Editing a narrative sentence down to hit a number is exactly the Lexile-driven editing R-KC-6 forbids.
